report.trigger: The third-party payment gateway had a burst of 503s. payment_gateway_5xx_rate went above zero at about 09:19:40Z and returned to zero at about 09:21:35Z. That fits the runbook's note that short gateway error bursts are normal and usually clear up in under two minutes.
report.root_cause: Deploy dep-8841 (commit a3f9c2e, 09:14:00–09:14:47Z) changed the retry policy in checkout/payment_client.py. It added 503 to status_forcelist, set allowed_methods=None (retry any method, including POST /charge) and set backoff_factor=0. As a result, each checkout sent up to 4 back-to-back charge attempts to the failing gateway. checkout-api holds its DB connection for the whole request, including those retries (runbook 'Connection handling contract'), so each failing checkout held a connection for 30–40 seconds. The 15-connection pool per instance (pool_size=5, max_overflow=10) filled up and stayed full from about 09:19:50Z to 09:21:00Z. After that, every endpoint sharing the pool timed out after 10 seconds waiting for a connection (pool_timeout=10) and returned 503.
report.failure_mode: On checkout-api-3, customers got generic 503s on every endpoint, not just checkout. That included read-only GET /cart and GET /orders/{id} pages, which never call the gateway. Checkout POSTs stalled: p95 latency was about 40s, against a baseline of about 215ms. Of 124 503s, 105 came from checkout-api's own DB connection-pool timeouts and only 19 were passed through from the gateway. checkout_5xx_rate peaked at about 70%.
contributing_factors: The DB connection is held through the external gateway call (an intentional atomic-transaction design). This ties how long connections are held to gateway latency and retries.
backoff_factor=0 fires retries immediately against a gateway that is already failing, with no Retry-After-style pause.
The pool is small (15 per instance), and read endpoints share it with checkout, so the checkout failure spread to cart and order pages.
allowed_methods=None makes non-idempotent POST charge calls retryable, which risks duplicate charges if the gateway does not deduplicate. This is a separate correctness risk.
ruled_out: The gateway alone as the cause of the outage: reverting only the retry policy with the burst still present gave 0 pool timeouts, 0 read-endpoint 503s and 0 seconds of pool saturation. The gateway explains checkout failures but not the outage across all endpoints.
A CPU or capacity problem: cpu_percent stayed around 30–37% throughout the incident (dashboard, confirmed as flat).

Simply undersized pool capacity: doubling the pool to 30 removed pool timeouts, but the pool was still saturated for 14 seconds and checkout p95 was still 37.9s. More capacity treats the symptom, not the retry amplification.

A general checkout-api bug from the deploy unrelated to the gateway: removing the gateway burst while keeping the new retry policy gave 0 503s and 226ms p95. The deploy is only harmful when the gateway fails.
My earlier draft report ('gateway outage', no replay) was wrong and is superseded by this one.
report.counterfactual_evidence: Deployed configuration (baseline replay): 124 503s (56 checkout POST, 68 reads), 105 pool_timeout, 19 gateway, pool saturated 76s, checkout p95 40,568ms, reads p95 10,000ms. Reverting the retry policy: 93 503s, all checkout-POST gateway 503s; 0 pool timeouts, 0 read 503s, 0s saturated, reads p95 49ms. Removing the gateway burst: 0 503s, p95 226ms. Releasing the connection before the gateway call: 33 503s (gateway only), 0 pool timeouts, 0s saturated, reads p95 49ms. Pool capacity 30: 33 503s, 0 pool timeouts, 14s saturated. The trigger (the burst) is necessary. The retry policy is what turns it into pool exhaustion and an outage across all endpoints. Note: reverting the retry policy led to more checkout-POST failures (93 vs 56), because retries do rescue some charges. The cost is taking down all other endpoints.
report.documentation_evidence: urllib3 Retry documentation (urllib3.readthedocs.io, util reference): by default only idempotent methods are retried, and allowed_methods set to 'a None value to retry on any verb'. status_forcelist forces a retry only when the method is in allowed_methods. Backoff is disabled by default (factor 0), so there is no sleep between retries. This is expected library behavior and was not observed in the incident itself.
evidence_citations: deploy dep-8841 diff: '+ status_forcelist={502, 503, 504}', '+ allowed_methods=None', '+ backoff_factor=0' (was {502,504}, {"GET"}, 0.5)

report.remaining_uncertainty: The evidence covers only checkout-api-3. The other 5 instances are assumed to behave the same way but were not inspected. The replay is a simulation of this traffic, not production. I did not check whether retried POST charges caused duplicate charges; that depends on gateway idempotency, which I have no evidence on. I did not look into why the gateway had the burst.
report.recommended_fix: Right away: roll back dep-8841 (kubectl rollout undo deployment/checkout-api), or restore allowed_methods={"GET"}, status_forcelist={502,504} and backoff_factor=0.5. Then: (1) Do not retry non-idempotent POST charges unless you send an idempotency key the gateway honors. (2) Release the DB connection before the gateway call and reacquire it to commit (the replay showed 0 pool timeouts), or put a strict total time budget on the payment call that stays well under pool_timeout. (3) Give read endpoints their own pool, separate from checkout. (4) Audit for duplicate charges during 09:19–09:22Z.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Deploy dep-8841 retry policy (503 retried, allowed_methods=None so POST retried, backoff 0) multiplied gateway 503-burst calls while the DB connection is held, exhausting the 15-connection pool; pool-timeout 503s then hit all endpoints.
hypotheses.supporting_evidence: req-01832: 4 POST charge attempts, 31.4s holding conn. 105 503_pool_timeout traces (checkout 37, cart 26, orders 42) vs 19 503_gateway; pool at 15 from ~09:19:50 to 09:21:00.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Root cause: dep-8841 retry policy (retry POST on 503, no backoff) combined with the connection held across the gateway call exhausted the DB pool during the gateway 503 burst, spreading 503s to read endpoints. The gateway burst was the trigger.
hypotheses.supporting_evidence: Baseline replay: 124 503s, 105 pool timeouts, 68 read 503s, 76s saturated. Revert retry: 0 pool timeouts, 0 read 503s, 0s saturated, 93 checkout gateway 503s. Remove burst: 0 503s. Release conn before gateway: 0 pool timeouts, 33 503s. Pool 30: 0 pool timeouts but still 14s saturated.
